title: Fundamental theorem of calculus, part II (evaluation rule), for a uniformly continuous integrand
statement: THE FUNDAMENTAL THEOREM OF CALCULUS, PART II -- THE EVALUATION RULE -- in the form a textbook states it: if G has derivative F on [a, b] (uniformly, in Bishop's sense) and F is uniformly continuous there, then the integral of F over [a, b] is equivalent to G(b) - G(a). The conclusion is CReal.Equiv, the Bishop-setoid equality on regular sequences, not Eq. G is ANY antiderivative, not the canonical CReal.antiderivative. NO side condition beyond uniform continuity: the (kb : Nat) and BoundedOn F a b kb that CReal.integral_eq_antideriv_diff demands of its caller are discharged from the uniform-continuity witness via CReal.bounded_of_uniformly_continuous, whose kb is COMPUTED, not obtained by Exists-elimination.

formal.statement: theorem CReal.integral_eq_antideriv_diff_of_uc : ((x0 : ((x0 : CReal) -> CReal)) -> ((x1 : ((x1 : CReal) -> CReal)) -> ((x2 : CReal) -> ((x3 : CReal) -> ((x4 : CReal.le x2 x3) -> ((x5 : CReal.UniformlyContinuousOn x0 x2 x3) -> ((x6 : CReal.HasDerivativeOn x1 x0 x2 x3) -> CReal.Equiv (CReal.integral x0 x2 x3 x4 x5) (CReal.add (x1 x3) (CReal.neg (x1 x2))))))))))

notes:
WHAT THIS ADDS, PRECISELY. CReal.integral_eq_antideriv_diff (landed 2026-08-27) already proves FTC-II; this fact is a STRENGTHENING OF ITS STATEMENT, arity 9 to arity 7, discharging a hypothesis that was always derivable from one already present.

NO MEAN VALUE THEOREM IS USED, AND THAT IS THE CONSTRUCTIVE POINT. The classical proof of the evaluation rule runs through the MVT, which is an existence statement and is not constructively available in that form (it is a separate roadmap item, W2-20). The route here avoids it entirely: G and the canonical antiderivative A are both antiderivatives of F, so G - A has derivative zero; CReal.constant_of_zero_deriv gives G a - A a = G b - A b; and A a = 0, A b = the integral, are both instances of the same degenerate-interval fact. What replaces the MVT is the UNIFORMITY of CReal.HasDerivativeOn: because the modulus is global on [a, b], the constancy of a zero-derivative function follows from a uniform estimate rather than from a point whose existence must be asserted.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY. It does not assert that an antiderivative EXISTS for an arbitrary F -- that is FTC-I (F:creal-hasderivative-antiderivative-of-uc), and it needs the uniform continuity hypothesis. It says nothing about improper integrals, unbounded intervals, or integrands that are merely pointwise continuous.
